state:
Goal `tools-server` is reached: every feature of the group `tools:server` has its proofs, and
`bun nv proofs --owed --group tools:server` lists none. `bun nv owners --closes tools-server` and
`bun nv playbook --closes tools-server` name nothing.

The floor check `nvs queue migrate creates both tables` was red because the Docker daemon had
restarted without the test servers, not because of the tree. `docker compose -f
tests/db/compose.yaml up -d --wait postgres redis mariadb mysql mssql` brought them back, and the
check's command prints both `applied` lines again. The playbook bullet *a floor check that passed
for sessions can go red because* owns the trap.

One proof of the group is a known gap: `tests/hostile/tools/server/nvs-serve/02-a-request-that-takes-all-the-memory.nvs`
carries the marker of `data/gaps/nvs-runtime/a-loop-that-only-concatenates-never-stops.json`.

The pack did not print the playbook bullet *an attack whose last step doubles a string in an
endless loop*, which this goal's `context` field `playbook` does not name.

next.note: nothing is open. The goal's one check, `bun nv proofs --verify --group tools:server`, has nothing owed.

backlog: `nvs run` with no `[limits] memory` in any configuration file stopped a string-doubling loop only when the allocator failed, at tens of gigabytes, with `memory allocation of … bytes failed`. Whether a command-line run is meant to have no ceiling was not checked; `crates/nvs-runtime/src/lib.rs`'s module doc owns the answer.

The summaries `nvs service --help` prints for `uninstall`, `status` and `unit`, and the long help of `--config`, are still written in the dense voice; `crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs:1085` holds them, and goal `plain-comments` is where that sweep belongs.
